summary: This note is a clipped Snowflake documentation page covering two SQL data generation functions, RANDSTR and RANDOM. RANDSTR returns a random string of a given length drawn from letters and digits, while RANDOM returns a pseudo-random 64-bit integer. The page explains the seed arguments, the usage caveats for repeated calls, the MT19937-64 algorithm, and includes example queries and outputs. Navigation menus, language links and footer boilerplate were ignored.
one_line: Snowflake SQL reference pages for the RANDSTR and RANDOM data generation functions, covering seeds, usage notes, and examples.
key_facts: RANDSTR(<length>, <gen>) returns a random string of the specified length.
RANDSTR chooses individual characters uniformly at random from the pool 0-9, a-z, A-Z.
The generator expression gen in RANDSTR is used as the seed for the uniform random distribution.
In the RANDSTR example with seed 1234, randstr(5, 1234) returned E5tav in all five generated rows.
RANDOM returns a pseudo-random 64-bit integer on each call.
RANDOM([seed]) takes an optional integer seed; if no seed is provided, a random seed is chosen in a platform-specific manner.
If a statement calls RANDOM with the same seed for each row, RANDOM returns a different value for each row.
If a statement calls RANDOM more than once with the same seed for the same row, it returns the same value for each call in that row.
There is no guarantee that a statement calling RANDOM produces the same set of values when executed more than once, with or without a seed.
Random values are not necessarily unique; the page recommends sequences SEQ1, SEQ2, SEQ4 or SEQ8 when unique values are needed.
The period of RANDOM before wrapping is 2^19937 - 1.
RANDOM implements a 64-bit Mersenne twister algorithm known as MT19937-64.
The output of RANDOM is only pseudo-random and can be predicted given enough information, including the algorithm and the seed.
Generating pseudo-random numbers with RANDOM is computationally expensive, so large numbers of calls can consume significant resources.
